text: dsh-terminal-vision 是一款面向 DSH 的终端交互工具插件，通过 PTY 会话和 @xterm/headless 将终端输出整理为可读屏幕文本、光标位置与当前行，并向 agent 注册终端工具。用户可开启持久会话、查看当前屏幕、发送普通文本或组合按键、读取滚屏历史、列出或关闭会话，适合需要操作 vim、htop 等交互式 TUI 的场景。运行需要 Node.js 及 node-pty、@xterm/headless 依赖；不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-terminal-vision gives DSH agents persistent PTY sessions and readable terminal screens. Agents can inspect screens, send keys, read scrollback, and manage sessions for interactive TUIs such as vim or htop. It requires Node.js with node-pty and @xterm/headless; no API key is needed.
想让 DSH agent 能查看并操作交互式终端界面。
需要在同一终端会话里反复发送按键并读取屏幕变化。
I want an agent to inspect terminal screens and recover output that has scrolled away.
dsh-terminal-vision 的功能「交互式终端会话」：开启一个持久 PTY 会话，可指定 shell 或直接运行 TUI 程序；之后可连续查看结构化屏幕、发送按键并在使用完毕后关闭会话。
dsh-terminal-vision 的功能「屏幕与滚屏读取」：读取当前可见文本、光标和活动行，也可查看终端滚屏区最近的若干行，便于 agent 获取超出当前视口的输出。
dsh-terminal-vision README · dsh-terminal-vision：**Terminal semantic vision plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-harness) (DSH).**

dsh-terminal-vision README · dsh-terminal-vision：Gives the agent "semantic vision" over interactive terminal programs — vim, htop, lazygit, less, setup TUIs — instead of a raw escape-sequence byte stream. Every PTY session is continuously parsed by [@xterm/headless](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js) (the headless JS port of xterm.js) into a structured **screen model**: visible text lines, cursor position, active line. The agent can then *read the screen*, *send keys*, *read again* — a perception/action loop over any TUI.

dsh-terminal-vision README · Tools registered in DSH：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `terminal_open(session_name, shell?, cwd?, cols?, rows?)` | Open a persistent PTY session, returns `session_id`. `shell` may be a shell name (`bash`, `pwsh`, `cmd`) **or** a TUI program to run directly (`htop`, `vim file.txt`). |
| `terminal_get_screen(session_id)` | Structured screen model: `lines[]`, `cursor {x, y}`, `active_line`, terminal title. |
| `terminal_send_keys(session_id, keys, wait_ms?)` | Send a key sequence and **wait for the screen to change** (readiness wait, default 500 ms), then return the new screen. Accepts plain text, named keys (`Enter`, `Esc`, `Up`…), modifiers (`Ctrl+C`, `Alt+b`), space-separated sequences (`":wq Enter"`). |
| `terminal_read_output(session_id, lines?)` | Last N lines of the scrollback buffer (history above the viewport). |
| `terminal_close(session_id)` | Close the session and free the PTY. |
| `terminal_list_sessions()` | List active sessions with id, name, shell, cwd, alive status. |

dsh-terminal-vision README · Architecture：- **Host part (TypeScript, `src/`)** — Cordis plugin: `apply(ctx)` registers the tools on `ctx.tools`, manages persistent sessions via **node-pty** (prebuilt ConPTY binaries on Windows — no compiler needed).
- **Semantic parser (`src/screen-model.ts`)** — **Variant A**: `@xterm/headless` builds the screen model natively in Node. Raw PTY output is written into a headless xterm Terminal; the buffer is read out on demand (`buffer.active`, `translateToString`). No Python, no long-lived bridge process, works offline.
- Keys are translated by `encodeKeys()` (friendly names → terminal bytes, including Ctrl/Alt modifiers, arrows, F-keys).
- Readiness wait: after each `terminal_send_keys`, the tool waits until the screen revision changes (data arrives) or the timeout elapses — preventing "blind" sends.
- All tools return JSON-serializable objects; unknown session ids return a clear error instead of crashing.
dsh-terminal-vision README · Install：```bash
dsh-terminal-vision README · from a local checkout：dsh plugin --profile web add file:./dsh-terminal-vision

dsh-terminal-vision README · or from GitHub：dsh plugin --profile web add github:fdfdfdfgbfdgfdg-star/dsh-terminal-vision
```

**Windows note:** pnpm blocks native-module install scripts by default. If the
add step fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: node-pty`, run the blocked build
step manually (node-pty ships prebuilt ConPTY binaries — no compiler needed):bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web
pnpm rebuild node-pty     # runs the postinstall that copies conpty.dll
```

dsh-terminal-vision README · or from GitHub：Then restart DSH (relaunch the DeepSeek Harness app, or re-run `dsh --profile web`)
and check the boot log for:

[terminal-vision] loaded: tools=6
```

Verify in a chat: "Какие инструменты терминала тебе доступны?" — the agent
should list the six `terminal_*` tools.

The package declares a `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`), so `dsh plugin add` wires the plugin into the profile automatically — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` edits needed.

dsh-terminal-vision README · Example session：```text
terminal_open(session_name="htop", shell="htop")     → session_id
terminal_get_screen(session_id)                      → lines[] of the htop interface, cursor
terminal_send_keys(session_id, "F10")                → quit htop, new screen
terminal_close(session_id)

Driving a shell:

dsh-terminal-vision README · Example session：```text
terminal_open(session_name="work", shell="bash")
terminal_send_keys(session_id, "ls -la\n")
terminal_get_screen(session_id)                      → the ls output
terminal_read_output(session_id, lines=200)          → anything that scrolled off

dsh-terminal-vision README · Build & test (development)：```bash
npm install
npm run build      # tsc → lib/
npm test           # node --test test/integration.test.js
```

dsh-terminal-vision README · Build & test (development)：`lib/` (compiled JS) is committed, so a plain `dsh plugin add` needs no build step. For the same reason the package deliberately has **no `prepare` script**: pnpm blocks git-hosted packages from running build scripts on install (`ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`), and since `lib/` is already in the repository the build is unnecessary. When developing, run `npm run build` and commit the updated `lib/`.

dsh-terminal-vision README · Dependencies：- **Node.js >= 22.19** (DSH host requirement)
- `node-pty` ^1.1.0 — ships prebuilt Windows ConPTY binaries; no Visual Studio Build Tools required on Windows 11
- `@xterm/headless` ^6.0.0 — pure JS, no native code
- No Python, no root/admin rights

dsh-terminal-vision README · Known limitations：- The screen model is text-only: colors/attributes are parsed by the emulator but not exposed in the snapshot.
- `cursorHidden` is advisory (xterm.js does not expose the DECTCEM state); most TUIs keep the cursor visible.
- `Alt+<letter>` sends ESC-prefixed bytes (application keypad mode not negotiated per-program).
- Sessions live in the DSH host process; restarting DSH closes all sessions.
- On Windows the default shell is `cmd.exe` (ConPTY); `bash` works if Git Bash / WSL bash is on PATH.
